key_insight: CoWA improves test-time adaptation for chest X-ray models by using disease co-occurrence patterns as a signal of which unlabeled predictions are more reliable.
clinical_relevance: This could help medical imaging systems stay more accurate after deployment at new hospitals where scanner settings, protocols, and patient mixes differ.
method: Estimates pathology co-occurrence structure from the model’s own predictions on target data.
Downweights samples that deviate from expected co-occurrence patterns.
Adapts the pretrained model using unlabeled target images while relying more on consistent predictions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on chest X-ray benchmarks under domain shifts, with consistent improvements over established test-time adaptation baselines.
watch_item: Because CoWA depends on predicted co-occurrence patterns, inaccurate early predictions or unusual local disease distributions could weaken adaptation or bias the weighting.
paper_title: Leveraging Pathology Co-occurrence for Test-Time Adaptation in Chest X-Ray Diagnosis
